chunks: Abu Ali al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar from Safwan ibn Yahya from Mansur ibn Hazim from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about a strip of land between two houses, and he claimed that Ali (peace be upon him) ruled in its favor for the owner of the house whose face [front] is towards the strip.

key_terms.خُصٍّ: A narrow strip of land or space

ai.seo_question: Who owns a narrow strip of land between two houses according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes a specific precedent in Shia jurisprudence regarding the ownership of a narrow strip of land (*khas*) between two properties, ruling it belongs to the owner whose house front faces the strip. This decision by Imam Ali (peace be upon him) highlights the principle of *qurb* (proximity) and practical access in property disputes, serving as a foundational case for determining rights in shared or ambiguous boundaries. It underscores the practical application of justice in urban property management during the early Islamic period.
